question: Add the term dyndns to the interface vocabulary (scripts/dossier/schema.json, the closed-set table of docs/conventions/README.md and the meaning of unknown in dossier/README.md), meaning an update URL, authenticated by a token or a per-record key, that changes the address (or the TXT value) of a record that already exists and creates, lists and deletes no record, zone or subdomain (DuckDNS can also clear the values of a record with clear=true); then set interface to dyndns on domains-dns/afraid-freedns, domains-dns/he-dns and domains-dns/cloudns-free (unknown now) and on domains-dns/duckdns (rest now). Review domains-dns/namecheap-freedns (rest) and egress/netassist-tb, egress/netassist-tunnelbroker, egress/tahio-tunnelbroker and egress/tunnel64 (cli), whose records name a dynamic-update URL beside the term they carry.
why: interface is the field a reader filters on for programmatic access: unknown, which dossier/README.md defines as no page says, hides a documented update path, and rest overstates an update-only call. All four records document the same capability and none documents a free-plan call that creates, lists or deletes a record: HE updates the IPv4 and IPv6 address of A and AAAA records through a simple web request or any dyndns compatible client, afraid.org offers a fetchable URL that auto-updates the network address, ClouDNS marks HTTP API access absent on Free and gives each A or AAAA record a DynURL, and DuckDNS takes one HTTPS GET that updates, or with clear=true clears, the values of named subnames. HE offers a /nic/update URL (and, by a third-party report, so does the afraid.org v2 interface) while DuckDNS, ClouDNS and the afraid.org token URL use their own shapes, so the term names the capability and not one protocol; ddns is the other plausible spelling. domains-dns/duckdns is measured, so a documented-rung set of its interface conflicts with the record and needs the rules session's own change (AGENTS.md section 2 rule 12).
